glossary.Palpitations: An unpleasant awareness of your own heartbeat.
glossary.Syncope: A brief loss of consciousness from reduced blood flow to the brain.
glossary.Ischaemic heart disease: Heart disease from narrowed coronary arteries reducing blood supply to the heart muscle.
glossary.Electrolyte imbalance: Abnormal blood levels of salts such as potassium, magnesium or calcium.
glossary.Structural heart disease: Abnormal heart anatomy, such as valve disease or cardiomyopathy.
glossary.JVP: Jugular venous pressure: the height of the pulse seen in the neck veins, reflecting right atrial pressure.
glossary.A wave: The JVP wave caused by right atrial contraction; absent in AF.
glossary.P wave: The ECG wave produced by atrial depolarisation.
glossary.QRS complex: The ECG wave produced by ventricular depolarisation.
glossary.Narrow-complex: QRS under 120 ms, meaning the impulse came through the normal conduction system.
glossary.Broad-complex: QRS over 120 ms, usually because the rhythm starts in the ventricles or conduction is abnormal.
glossary.Paroxysmal: Coming and going in sudden episodes.
glossary.Isoelectric line: The flat baseline of the ECG between waves.
glossary.Polymorphic: Changing in shape from beat to beat.
glossary.First-degree heart block: A PR interval over 200 ms with every P wave still followed by a QRS.
glossary.Mobitz I: Second-degree heart block where the PR lengthens until a QRS is dropped; also called Wenckebach.
glossary.Shock: Inadequate blood flow to the organs, usually with low blood pressure.
glossary.Myocardial ischaemia: Heart muscle not getting enough oxygen.
glossary.Asystole: No electrical activity in the heart: a flat line on the ECG.
glossary.Rheumatic fever: An immune reaction after streptococcal throat infection that can damage the heart valves.
glossary.Macrolide: An antibiotic class, such as clarithromycin and azithromycin, that can prolong the QT interval.
glossary.Clarithromycin: A macrolide antibiotic that prolongs the QT interval.
glossary.Azithromycin: A macrolide antibiotic that can prolong the QT interval.
glossary.SSRIs: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors: antidepressants such as citalopram; some prolong the QT interval.
glossary.Citalopram: An SSRI antidepressant known to prolong the QT interval.
glossary.Anti-epileptic: A drug used to prevent seizures.
glossary.Hypothermia: Core body temperature below 35 degrees C.
glossary.QT interval: Time from the start of the Q wave to the end of the T wave: ventricular depolarisation plus repolarisation.
glossary.Morphology: The shape of the ECG waves.
glossary.Notched: Having a small dip or split in the wave, as in the M-shaped R wave of LBBB.
glossary.RSR': A QRS with two upward peaks (M shape) in V1, typical of RBBB.
glossary.Dominant S wave: A QRS that is mainly downward, as in V1 in LBBB.
glossary.ST depression: The ST segment sitting below the baseline on the ECG.
glossary.Echocardiogram: An ultrasound scan of the heart showing its structure and pumping function.
glossary.Bloods: Blood tests, here including electrolytes, thyroid function and full blood count.
glossary.TE: Thromboembolism: a clot that has travelled and blocked a vessel.
glossary.Hb: Haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells.
glossary.eGFR: Estimated glomerular filtration rate: a measure of kidney function.
glossary.Anticoagulation: Using drugs that thin the blood to prevent clots.
glossary.Rate control: Slowing the ventricular rate in AF without trying to restore sinus rhythm.
glossary.Rhythm control: Trying to restore and keep normal sinus rhythm, with drugs or cardioversion.
glossary.Beta-blocker: A drug blocking adrenaline at beta receptors, slowing the heart; avoid in asthma.
glossary.Non-dihydropyridine CCB: A calcium channel blocker such as verapamil or diltiazem that slows the heart rate.
glossary.Carotid sinus massage: Pressing over the carotid sinus in the neck to stimulate the vagus nerve and slow the heart.
glossary.Sinus bradycardia: Normal sinus rhythm but under 60 bpm.
glossary.Adrenaline: A hormone and drug that increases heart rate and contractility.
glossary.Temporary pacing: Short-term electrical stimulation of the heart while waiting for a permanent fix.
glossary.Transcutaneous pacing: Pacing through pads on the chest skin.
glossary.Transvenous pacing: Pacing through a wire passed through a vein into the heart.
glossary.Permanent pacemaker: An implanted device that sends electrical impulses to keep the heart beating at a safe rate.
glossary.Accessory pathway: An extra electrical connection between atria and ventricles that bypasses the AV node.
glossary.Sotalol: A beta-blocker with extra anti-arrhythmic action; prolongs the QT interval.
glossary.Secondary prevention: Treatment to stop a disease event happening again after it has already occurred.
glossary.Magnesium sulphate: IV magnesium used to treat torsades de pointes by stabilising the cardiac membrane.
glossary.Ischaemic stroke: Stroke caused by a blocked artery to the brain.
glossary.Aspirin: An antiplatelet drug that stops platelets clumping.
glossary.Automaticity: The ability of heart cells to fire impulses on their own.
glossary.Ectopic pacemaker: A group of heart cells outside the sinus node that starts firing impulses.
glossary.AV node: The atrioventricular node: the electrical gateway delaying impulses between atria and ventricles.
glossary.Repolarisation: Heart cells resetting their electrical charge after each beat.
glossary.Cardiac output: The volume of blood the heart pumps per minute.
glossary.Defibrillation: An unsynchronised electric shock to stop VF or pulseless VT.
glossary.AV dissociation: Atria and ventricles beating independently of each other.
glossary.Thrombus: A blood clot formed inside a vessel or heart chamber.
glossary.Embolise: When a clot breaks off and travels to block a vessel elsewhere.
glossary.Stasis: Slow or still blood flow, which encourages clotting.
